newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian undertaker offers death at a discount.
newsitem.headline: Italian undertaker offers death at a discount.

text.p: An Italian undertaker is trying to drum up business with discounts for death on the cheap.
The news agency AGI on Saturday said the firm in the Sicilian town of Syracuse had printed fake 100,000 lire banknotes and dropped them in the streets as publicity.

One side reads "Maybe you've got a 99-year-old aunt. If you want to save a lot of 100,000 lire banknotes turn over." The other side gives the name of the firm adding: "No to dear death. It costs less to change worlds with us".
AGI said some Sicilians were keeping the bills for fun but many had thrown them away after making a traditional sign of superstition with their fingers to ward off evil.
A real 100,000 lire note is worth about $60.
